storeProposal.choice: KEEP Neon Postgres (PostgresRateLimitStore on existing MCP DATABASE_URL / rate_limit_counters). Do not re-provision Upstash. Do not add Memorystore. Do not add a new third-party.
storeProposal.whyNotUpstash: Dead DB is the regression. Re-provisioning Upstash adds a third-party Redis the Vercel→GCP migration (P-34) would immediately strand. REST client remains in-tree as a legacy adapter behind HAUSKA_RATE_LIMIT_STORE=upstash; production must not select it.
storeProposal.whyNotMemorystore: Requires VPC connector + persistent TCP from Cloud Run + a new billed GCP service. MCP already has a working Neon pool. Memorystore is the right long-term GCP Redis if C4 proves hot-path cost on Neon; not justified for a regression restore.
storeProposal.whyPostgres: Already merged (hauska-mcp-server #58 @ 9ab0247), migration 010 applied, serving 00042-25d live-probes rate_limit_store.state=ok detail=postgres. Durable across deploys, shared across replicas, sits on the Neon the GCP migration already owns. Zero new vendor.

costs.upstashReprovision: new vendor account + secret rotation + REST hop; stranded by P-34
costs.memorystore: VPC connector + Redis instance monthly; new dependency
costs.postgresKeep: counter upserts on existing MCP Neon; T4 burst already proved shared budget on 00040-ctj; hot-path cost is one upsert per window per identity — acceptable at launch rpm

failureModes.neonBlip: ResilientRateLimitStore fail-degrades to per-instance memory; /health rate_limit_store.state becomes degraded; budgets split across replicas until primary recovers
failureModes.tableMissing: startup catch → memory primary + production error log rate_limit_store_env_missing; health degraded
failureModes.upstashSelectedByEnv: placeholder URL throws; same memory fallback. Mitigate by pinning HAUSKA_RATE_LIMIT_STORE=postgres in cloudbuild-mcp.yaml

outageMode.meaning: On store outage, requests continue against per-instance MemoryRateLimitStore. /health reports rate_limit_store.state="degraded" with memory_fallback=true and outage_policy="fail-degraded". Never state="ok" on memory. Never a silent skip.
outageMode.whyNotFailClosed: Fail-closed would 503 the public MCP gate on a Neon blip and take Layer-1 free agents offline. The gate's job during an outage is to stay up and scream, not to go dark.
outageMode.healthSignal: dependencies.rate_limit_store.state plus explicit primary / memory_fallback / outage_policy fields (this lane's code change). /health HTTP stays 200 (liveness). /health/ready does NOT treat rate_limit_store as critical (existing design: only engine_retrieval_api + postgres DOWN → 503).
outageMode.silentFallbackForbidden: The current memory fallback may remain ONLY as this explicitly-surfaced degraded mode. A health body that reports ok while serving memory is the defect class this program hunts.
